proof.text:
Use the constant-ring structure identifications throughout. They are the canonical isomorphisms preserving constant sections, so the module pullbacks are the inverse images in the comparison theorems. Finite $q,r$ are proper, so the etale proper/open theorem applies. Its coefficient hypothesis holds because $\Lambda$ is finite, hence torsion. For $s=e,p$ write $\iota^s_j:1\to j_s^*j_{s,!}$ for the OPEN-extension unit (distinct from the ordinary pullback/direct-image unit). All comparison pullbacks and open extensions used here are exact; the comparison preserves bounded-below objects. Thus the sheaf open-comparison unit identity of the cited normalization theorem holds termwise on complexes and then in $D^+$, with the same named maps:
$$j_p^*(e_{j,F})\circ a_{j,j_{e,!}F}\circ C_U(\iota^e_{j,F})=\iota^p_{j,C_UF}.\tag{1}$$
Indeed naturality makes this a chain-map identity in each degree, and localization preserves compositions and equalities. The same formula holds for $j'$.

source.place: Tag 09AF, lemma-jshriek-comparison (canonical adjoint comparison); extension of its open-unit normalization degreewise; finite properness Tag 01WN

proof.text:
Set $X_N=j'_{e,!}N$, $M_N=Rr_{e,*}N$, and let $E^e_X:j_e^*Rq_{e,*}X\to Rr_{e,*}j_e'^*X$ be ordinary etale exchange for this open square. Open derived restriction identifies this named map with restriction: on a K-injective representative $I$ of $X_N$ the derived exchange is the underived exchange $j_e^{-1}q_{e,*}I\to r_{e,*}j_e'^{-1}I$ in each degree ($r$ is finite, so $r_{e,*}$ is exact and computes $Rr_{e,*}$), and the underived exchange along the open (etale) base change $j$ is, on sections, the identity $I(V\times_ZZ')=I(V\times_UU')$, an isomorphism. Put
$$\delta^e_N=Rr_{e,*}((\iota^e_{j',N})^{-1})\circ E^e_{X_N}:j_e^*Rq_{e,*}X_N\xrightarrow{\sim}M_N.$$
Here the open unit is an isomorphism: for a module sheaf on $U'$, restriction of the defining extension-by-zero presheaf has value $F(V)$ at every etale $V\to U'$; its sheafification is already $F$, and the unit sends $s$ to $s$. This is the same module adjunction specified in the cited theorem. For complexes this description is degreewise, since both open functors are exact. Open derived restriction and this unit isomorphism show that $\delta^e_N$ is invertible.

source.place: Tag 0D6G, lemma-restrict-direct-image-open; extension-by-zero unit computed on the open subsite

proof.text:
The proper-support-normalized $\gamma^e_N$ has open-adjunction transpose $(\delta^e_N)^{-1}$. Check the normalization as follows. Finite direct image is exact on abelian etale sheaves, hence also on constant-$\Lambda$ module sheaves: direct image commutes with forgetting the action by evaluation, and the underlying kernels and sheafified cokernels compute module kernels and cokernels. The exact-functor derived comparison therefore computes $Rr_{e,*}$ and $Rq_{e,*}$ termwise. On the K-injective representative $J$ in the proper/open theorem, its map $j_{e,!}r_*J\cong q_*j'_{e,!}J\to q_*I$ is consequently the termwise proper-support identification, followed by the canonical resolution isomorphism. On an etale test object $V\to U$, restriction of this first identification sends a section of $N(V\times_UU')$ to the identical section on $V\times_ZZ'\cong V\times_UU'$; all these objects lie in the open, so the open units also send each section to itself. The unit--counit ordinary exchange is this same restriction map: by the underived etale exchange-restriction theorem, applied degreewise to $j'_{e,!}J$ for the Cartesian square of $q$ and the open $j$, it is on sections the identity $(j'_{e,!}J)(V\times_ZZ')=(j'_{e,!}J)(V\times_UU'\to Z')$. Applying the identity in every degree gives
$$\delta^e_N\circ j_e^*(\gamma^e_N)\circ\iota^e_{j,M_N}=1_{M_N}.\tag{2}$$

source.place: Tag 0F7B, lemma-shriek-proper-and-open, defining K-injective representative; Tag 03QP, etale-cohomology-proposition-finite-higher-direct-image-zero

proof.text:
Let $E^p$ be ambient pro-etale exchange for the same square, and put
$$\delta^p_N=Rr_{p,*}((\iota^p_{j',C_{U'}N})^{-1})\circ E^p_{j'_{p,!}C_{U'}N}.$$
The pro-etale open unit is invertible directly from extension by zero and restriction: on every object over $U'$, extension followed by restriction has the original module sections and its unit is the identity. By the statement's defining transpose convention,
$$j_p^*(\gamma^p_{C_{U'}N})\circ\iota^p_{j,Rr_{p,*}C_{U'}N}=(\delta^p_N)^{-1}.$$
For the comparison calculation, apply the transport-identifies-exchange theorem with $f=q$, $f'=r$, $g=j$, $g'=j'$ and input $X=X_N$. All its hypotheses hold: $q,r$ are qcqs, the square is Cartesian, $X_N$ is bounded below because $j'_{e,!}$ is exact, and the coefficient is the finite constant ring fixed in Step 1. Its equation is precisely
$$E^p_{C_{Z'}X}\circ j_p^*(b_{q,X})\circ a_{j,Rq_{e,*}X}
=Rr_{p,*}(a_{j',X})\circ b_{r,j_e'^*X}\circ C_U(E^e_X).\tag{3}$$
It concerns the specified unit--counit exchanges and counit-mate $b$ of this item.

source.place: Tags 099R and 09AF; unit--counit comparison calculation using the named exchange theorem

proof.text:
Expand $T_N=Rq_{p,*}(e_{j',N})\circ b_{q,X_N}$. Naturality of $E^p$ at $e_{j',N}:C_{Z'}X_N\to j'_{p,!}C_{U'}N$, followed by (3), gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\delta^p_N\circ j_p^*T_N\circ a_{j,Rq_{e,*}X_N}
={}&Rr_{p,*}\bigl((\iota^p_{j',C_{U'}N})^{-1}\circ j_p'^*(e_{j',N})\circ a_{j',X_N}\bigr)\\
&\qquad\circ b_{r,j_e'^*X_N}\circ C_U(E^e_{X_N}).
\end{aligned}$$
By (1) for $j'$, the parenthesized morphism is $C_{U'}((\iota^e_{j',N})^{-1})$. Naturality of $b_r$ at $(\iota^e_{j',N})^{-1}$ now makes the right side $b_{r,N}\circ C_U(\delta^e_N)$. Thus
$$\delta^p_N\circ j_p^*T_N\circ a_{j,Rq_{e,*}X_N}=b_{r,N}\circ C_U(\delta^e_N).\tag{4}$$
This also proves invertibility of $\delta^p_N$ on the input at issue: $T_N$, $a_j$, $b_r$ and $C_U(\delta^e_N)$ are isomorphisms. Invertibility of the specified $b$ comes from its canonical-mate theorem, and that of $e$ from the open-comparison theorem.

source.place: Tag 09AF, canonical adjoint comparison; explicit substitution of equations (1) and (3) and naturality

proof.text:
For clarity compare maps whose source is $j_{p,!}C_UM_N$. Put
$$G_N=T_N\circ C_Z(\gamma^e_N)\circ e_{j,M_N}^{-1}:
 j_{p,!}C_UM_N\longrightarrow Rq_{p,*}j'_{p,!}C_{U'}N.$$
Its transpose under $j_{p,!}\dashv j_p^*$ is
$$g_N=j_p^*(G_N)\circ\iota^p_{j,C_UM_N}.$$
Equation (1), with $F=M_N$, rewrites this as
$$g_N=j_p^*T_N\circ j_p^*C_Z(\gamma^e_N)\circ a_{j,j_{e,!}M_N}\circ C_U(\iota^e_{j,M_N}).$$
Naturality of $a_j$ at $\gamma^e_N$ moves $a_j$ to its target. Postcomposing by $\delta^p_N$, then using (4) and (2), gives the explicit calculation
$$\begin{aligned}
\delta^p_N\circ g_N
&=b_{r,N}\circ C_U\bigl(\delta^e_N\circ j_e^*(\gamma^e_N)\circ\iota^e_{j,M_N}\bigr)\\
&=b_{r,N}.
\end{aligned}$$
Therefore $g_N=(\delta^p_N)^{-1}\circ b_{r,N}$.

source.place: Tag 09AF, canonical open adjunction; explicit transpose calculation from (1), (2), and (4)

proof.text:
The transpose of $\gamma^p_{C_{U'}N}\circ j_{p,!}(b_{r,N})$ under that same adjunction is also $(\delta^p_N)^{-1}\circ b_{r,N}$. Indeed naturality of its open unit gives
$$j_p^*j_{p,!}(b_{r,N})\circ\iota^p_{j,C_UM_N}
=\iota^p_{j,Rr_{p,*}C_{U'}N}\circ b_{r,N},$$
and the defining transpose of $\gamma^p$ then gives the assertion. Injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijection implies
$$\gamma^p_{C_{U'}N}\circ j_{p,!}(b_{r,N})
=T_N\circ C_Z(\gamma^e_N)\circ e_{j,M_N}^{-1}.$$
Postcompose on the source with $e_{j,M_N}$ to obtain exactly $\gamma^p_{C_{U'}N}\circ S_N=T_N\circ C_Z(\gamma^e_N)$, with $S_N,T_N$ as in the statement.

source.place: Tag 09AF and extension-by-zero adjunction; naturality of the unit and injectivity of its Hom bijection

proof.text:
Finally $S_N$ and $T_N$ are isomorphisms, since their factors are the canonical comparison isomorphisms. The etale map $\gamma^e_N$ is an isomorphism by the proper/open theorem, applied to proper $q,r$, open $j,j'$, finite $\Lambda$ and bounded-below $N$ as checked in Steps 1–2. The proved equality yields
$$\gamma^p_{C_{U'}N}=T_N\circ C_Z(\gamma^e_N)\circ S_N^{-1},$$
a composite of isomorphisms. This proves the final assertion as well.

title: Site comparison preserves finite proper/open interchange
statement:
Fix a finite commutative ring $\Lambda$. Use ordinary bounded-below derived categories of constant-$\Lambda$ modules on small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $C_T=\nu_T^*$ for the exact site comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. For a qcqs morphism $u:U\to V$ write $a_u:C_Uu_e^*\xrightarrow{\sim}u_p^*C_V$ for the canonical pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], $b_u:C_VRu_{e,*}\xrightarrow{\sim}Ru_{p,*}C_U$ for its counit-mate direct-image comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate], and for an open immersion $j$ write $e_j:C j_{e,!}\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{p,!}C$ for the canonical adjoint open-extension comparison [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison, def-cbc-finite-constant-coefficient-transport]. Subscripts $e,p$ distinguish the two sites. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$, $j':U'\hookrightarrow Z'$, $r:U'\to U$ and $q:Z'\to Z$ form a Cartesian square [def-cbc-open-immersion-square]. Assume all corners are Noetherian (each has a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]), $r,q$ are finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and all arrows are qcqs. Let $\gamma^e:j_{e,!}Rr_{e,*}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_{e,*}j'_{e,!}$ be the proper-support-normalized map [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence]. On the pro-etale site let $\gamma^p:j_{p,!}Rr_{p,*}\to Rq_{p,*}j'_{p,!}$ be the canonical map whose $j_{p,!}\dashv j_p^*$ transpose is the inverse of the open base-change isomorphism $j_p^*Rq_{p,*}j'_{p,!}\cong Rr_{p,*}j_p'^*j'_{p,!}\cong Rr_{p,*}$, using the ordinary unit--counit exchange and the open-extension unit [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations, def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange, lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. For every $N\in D^+(U'_e,\Lambda)$ define
$$S_N=j_{p,!}(b_{r,N})\circ e_{j,Rr_{e,*}N},\qquad T_N=Rq_{p,*}(e_{j',N})\circ b_{q,j'_{e,!}N}.$$
Then
$$\gamma^p_{C_{U'}N}\circ S_N=T_N\circ C_Z(\gamma^e_N),$$
and $\gamma^p_{C_{U'}N}$ is an isomorphism.
